claim.claim: Tesla's energy generation and storage revenue for fiscal year 2025 increased by more than 20% compared with fiscal year 2024.

verdict.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Tesla's energy generation and storage revenue for fiscal year 2025 increased by more than 20% compared with fiscal year 2024. 

Evidence E1 discusses cost of energy generation and storage revenue (not revenue itself), stating: "Cost of energy generation and storage revenue increased $1.52 billion, or 20%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024." This is about costs, not revenue.

Evidence E4 mentions "Energy generation and storage revenue includes sales, leasing, and financing of energy generation and storage products..." but does not provide the actual revenue figures or growth rate for FY2025 vs FY2024.

Evidence E2 provides partial year data: "Energy generation and storage revenue increased $870 million, or 19%, in the six months ended June 30, 2025 as compared to the six months ended June 30, 2024." This is only for six months, not the full fiscal year.

Evidence E6 provides nine-month data: "Energy generation and storage revenue increased $1.04 billion, or 44%, in the three months ended September 30, 2025" but this is comparing Q3 2025 to Q3 2024, not full year figures.

None of the evidence passages provide the actual full-year energy generation and storage revenue growth rate for FY2025 vs FY2024. While we have cost growth (20%) and partial year revenue growth rates (19% for H1, 44% for Q3), we do not have the complete full-year revenue growth figure needed to verify whether it exceeded 20%.
